title: Fixed or Floating Bearing Assignment
description: Ten scenario cards ask which bearing configuration a fan needs; after each commit the sim marks the drive-end and non-drive-end bearings fixed or floating on a shaft drawing and names the FanPedia rule step that decided the card.
creator: Twin City Fan
subject: fixed bearing
floating bearing
fixed-floating bearing rules
drive end bearing
non-drive end bearing
rights: Copyright 2026 Twin City Fan. All rights reserved.

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
learningObjectives: The learner will apply the fixed-floating bearing rules to assign the correct bearing configuration to ten fan scenarios defined by mounting orientation, bearing type, operating temperature and arrangement, with at least 8 of 10 correct.
prerequisites: ball, roller and split roller bearing types

accessibility.notes: describe() text (fallback mode); selections, verdicts with the fixed/floating result for each bearing, each new card and the summary announced through FP.announce (aria-live); ✓/✗ glyphs, bold text and solid/dashed borders pair with colour; the choice buttons are aria-pressed toggles; keys 1-4 or A-D choose, Enter commits and goes on; every button is reachable with Tab.

controls.label: A / B / C / D
controls.purpose: Choose a bearing configuration (keys 1-4 or A-D)

controls.label: Commit
controls.purpose: Lock in the chosen configuration (Enter); one attempt

controls.label: Next card / See results
controls.purpose: Go to the next card or the summary (Enter)

controls.label: Start over
controls.purpose: Reset all ten cards and the score

rules: Step 1: operating temperature >= 301 F gives one fixed and one floating bearing; go to step 3
Step 2: <= 300 F ball bearings give A (two fixed), except Arrangements 3SI, 7SI, 3DI and 7DI, which give D (engineering review); roller and split roller give one fixed and one floating
Step 3: with a floating bearing, horizontal mount gives B (fixed at the drive end) and vertical mount gives C (floating at the drive end)
limitations: FanPedia states these rules as guidelines; the straddle-arrangement footnote is an engineering review item, not a lookup
The shaft drawing is schematic; vertical fans are drawn with the drive end at the top

sources: Source: FanPedia pp. 97-99 (Bearings: Fixed & Floating Bearings), retrieved 2026-10-08
Source: FanPedia p. 91 (drive end and non-drive end bearings), retrieved 2026-10-08

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Apply a decision procedure to new cases, commit, then see the physical layout and the deciding rule step
keyQuestions: When does a fan need a floating bearing at all?
Why does the floating bearing move to the drive end on a vertical fan?
commonMisconceptions: Every fan needs a floating bearing
The fixed bearing is always on the drive end, regardless of orientation
Temperature does not matter for ball bearings
The 300 F cutoff applies the same way to straddle arrangements with ball bearings
assessmentOpportunities: Running score shown as 'Cards correct: n of 10'; mastery is 8 of 10 on the first attempt.
